title: Modeled Chicago and Auckland outdoor lamp mixtures for October–November 2026

source.credit: Route Replay modeled example, informed by Chicago Infrastructure Trust and Auckland Transport
source.notes: The authored model is MIT licensed; linked source publications retain their publishers' rights. Region sources describe streetlight programs, not measured citywide luminous mixtures. This profile is opt-in and applies only during the stated 2026 interval.

source.credit: Chicago Infrastructure Trust, April 21, 2017 streetlight modernization announcement
source.notes: Reference only; no article text or asset is redistributed. The announcement specifies LEDs at 3000 K or below to replace high-pressure sodium. It does not establish a measured 2026 lamp inventory or give permission to relicense the publication.

regions.notes: The 10/15/75 percent luminous weights are illustrative, not fixture counts or measured 2026 proportions. Carrying the 2017 program's warm-LED direction into these trip dates is a modeling assumption. The 20 km city-centered circle and district variation are synthetic, not municipal or road boundaries; ORD is outside it. Streetlight evidence informs only an outdoor-population proxy. Building, sign, persistent colors, population shares and schedules retain defaults.

source.credit: Auckland Transport, Sustainability: LED streetlight conversion
source.notes: AT reports 99% of its streetlight network converted to LED by mid-2025 and describes 4000 K LEDs. This concerns AT's network, not all city lights; the fixture percentage is not a measured luminous fraction. Publisher terms apply to the source publication.

regions.notes: The 1/99 percent luminous weights are an illustrative translation of the network conversion report, not calibrated radiance or a measured 2026 inventory. Assuming continued LED dominance during these trip dates is modeled. The 15 km city-centered circle and district variation are synthetic, not network boundaries; AKL is outside it. Only the outdoor-population proxy changes. Buildings, signs, persistent colors, population shares and schedules retain defaults.
